acceptance: Current/no-op and core-behind cases consume only trustworthy verified fork deliveries; wrong producer/run/digest/expected identity refuses without consulting upstream source or mutating the fork.

Tests cover duplicate polls, interrupted push/PR/merge, tooling-only movement, bursts of newer deliveries, preserved green/armed work, human disarm/hold, reverted-delivery suppression and explicitly authorized retry.

Candidate preparation has no write/reviewer secrets; allowed-path/hash checks precede publication. Scoped App identity is used for publication and arming, with actual ordinary PR/trunk triggers proven during activation.
Core dry-run is mutation-free and kill switch halts mutations without removing PRs; ordinary exact-head review/CI/pr-arm controls remain enforced.
Core updater PR passes normal review/CI and merges; live develop pin/archive hash confirms the accepted delivery after protected landing, never a fictional success issue.
context: Owner instruction 2026-11-05 supersedes BOTH rejected designs. benchbox-sqlglot owns upstream discovery/integration, fork PR lifecycle, source/relocation/runtime/engine/distribution validation and trustworthy wheel delivery. BenchBox core owns consuming that delivery, origin/identity/hash binding, transactional pin updates, its own wrapper/benchmark-definition/installed-package concerns and ordinary core PR landing. Core must not discover upstream, merge fork PRs, reconstruct/re-review fork source, repeat fork test matrices or acquire a fork-write credential. Theseus stays unchanged and generic; no special policy, external-source inlet, synthetic dataset, second model-review path or reviewer release is needed. Theseus PR25 closed unmerged; prior approval claims withdrawn. This supersedes the source-review-at-core portion of sqlglot-fork-review-h1-governance, not existing protected-branch rules or ordinary review requirements. Preserve exact merged-SHA producer evidence, scoped independent credentials, no candidate execution with write/reviewer secrets, no golden/outcome/test/waiver changes, reviewed rollback, human holds/disarms, reverted-delivery suppression and no public release/cloud spend. Update current fork/core runbooks to this boundary. Corrected proposal: local://sqlglot-end-to-end-proposal.md. The live tracker, not discarded branch code or prior notes, owns delivery state.
description:
Implement a narrow BenchBox core updater. Poll the fork verified-delivery contract plus manual dispatch; compare eligible version to the core pin, download exact artifact, verify trusted producer origin/expected identities/hash, use the transactional adopter and open an ordinary allowed-path core PR. Core never discovers upstream, prepares source refreshes, merges fork PRs, repeats fork validation or receives fork-write credentials. Upstream/build/producer exceptions belong in the fork; core wrapper/install/adoption exceptions belong in core. Theseus reviews the actual consumer PR normally, with no external-source mode or second review job.

Keep at most one core adoption active, preserve green/armed work across newer deliveries, remember reverted forkSHA+wheelHash so a poll cannot undo rollback, and never override a human disarm/hold. Only documented trunk-red disarm/recovery may be re-armed automatically. Separate no-write candidate preparation from pinned trusted publisher/arming code; core App has contents+PR write, no statuses/checks/workflows write. App-created and App-armed merges must trigger ordinary PR and trunk CI. Keep existing pr-arm exact-head/threads/holds/trunk/duration/review controls. Default-off kill switch, no-write dry-run and idempotent interrupted publication/merge handling. No new service, fork source review, source reconstruction, alternate builder or hidden retry-until-green.
